title: The Everett Interpretation of Quantum Mechanics: Many Worlds or None?
"Relative State" Formulation of Quantum Mechanics
container-title: The Many Worlds Interpretation of Quantum Mechanics

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>It is argued that the only way to avoid the “spooky action at a distance” of quantum mechanics is to accept the existence of parallel worlds created at every quantum measurement. Einstein’s boxes though experiment and the Greenberger–Horne–Zeilinger setup are analyzed within the framework of the many-worlds interpretation. It is shown that at the level of the universe—which encompasses all worlds—performing a measurement or any other action in one location does not lead to changes in the local properties of remote locations. Conversely, within the framework of single-world interpretations, such as Bohmian mechanics and the Ghirardi–Rimini–Weber collapse theory, measurements at one local site alter local properties at another. Einstein’s boxes example explicitly demonstrates the action at a distance inherent in collapse theories. While Bohmian mechanics can provide a local explanation for Einstein’s boxes, it cannot locally explain the outcome correlations of spin measurements in Greenberger–Horne–Zeilinger experiments. The central argument relies on the paradigm of a physical theory according to which a complete description everywhere at a given moment in time dictates what will happen everywhere in the future.</jats:p>
title: The Many-Worlds Interpretation of Quantum Mechanics Is the Only Way to Avoid Action at a Distance
